title: React State & Data Flow Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision of how data moves through a React app: props vs state, useState, immutable updates, lifting state, controlled inputs and context basics.

chapters.title: Props, State and One-Way Flow
points: Props: read-only inputs passed from parent to child; the child must never mutate them
State: data owned by a component that changes over time and triggers a re-render when updated
Rule of thumb: if it can be derived from props or other state, don't store it as state
One-way data flow: data goes down via props, events go up via callback props
Mental model: UI = f(props, state); a re-render re-runs the function with new values

chapters.title: useState and Immutable Updates
points: const [value, setValue] = useState(initial) returns the current value and a setter; initial is used only on the first render
Updating state schedules a re-render; the variable in the current render keeps its old value (state is a snapshot)
Use the updater form setCount(c => c + 1) when the new value depends on the previous one; this avoids stale values in batched updates
Never mutate objects/arrays in state: React compares with Object.is, so a mutated reference doesn't re-render
Immutable patterns: object {...obj, key: v}; add [...arr, item]; remove arr.filter(x => x.id !== id); edit arr.map(x => x.id === id ? {...x, done: true} : x)

chapters.title: Lifting State Up
points: When two siblings need the same data, move the state to their closest common parent
Parent passes the value down as a prop and a setter or handler down as a callback prop
Child calls the callback to ask the parent to change state; the parent stays the single source of truth
Don't duplicate lifted state in a child via useState(props.value): the copy ignores later prop changes
If lifting means passing props through many layers (prop drilling), consider context or composition

chapters.title: Controlled vs Uncontrolled Inputs
points: Controlled input: value and onChange are bound to state, so React is the source of truth: <input value={v} onChange={e => setV(e.target.value)} />
Uncontrolled input: the DOM holds the value; read it with a ref (ref.current.value) or on submit via FormData; use defaultValue for the initial value
Comparison: controlled suits live validation, formatting and conditionally disabling submit; uncontrolled suits simple forms and file inputs
Setting value without onChange makes the field read-only and logs a warning
Switching an input from undefined to a defined value flips it from uncontrolled to controlled; always initialise state to '' not undefined

chapters.title: Context Basics
points: Context passes data to any descendant without prop drilling: createContext(default), <Ctx.Provider value={x}>, useContext(Ctx)
useContext returns the value of the nearest Provider above it; the default applies only when there is no Provider
Every consumer re-renders when the Provider's value changes by reference, so memoise object values with useMemo or split contexts
Context is not state: pair it with useState/useReducer in the Provider, and put the value and setter in it
Good fits: theme, current user, locale; poor fit: rapidly changing data like form input or mouse position

chapters.title: State and Data Flow Cheat Sheet
points: Props down, events up; props are read-only, state is owned and changes trigger re-renders
Setter rules: updater form when depending on previous state; replace, never mutate; state is a snapshot per render
Immutable cheats: spread for objects, [...arr, x] to add, filter to remove, map to edit
Where state lives: one component -> local useState; siblings -> lift to common parent; many distant consumers -> context
Inputs: controlled = value + onChange; uncontrolled = ref/defaultValue; initialise to '' and never switch modes
